name: mood-curtain
does: On the cue word the new look falls top-down like a curtain (the previous look lifts away with a light hem on its edge, the face dark by the second frame), then the vignette closes in and film grain moves every frame until B.
use_when: a look change that should feel like a drop ('make it moody', 'the colours go dark', 'and then it hits'), best after a held pause
inputs: a GRADES entry for the new look from the curtain's first frame (or earlier) to B or later
the cue (T.cue: seconds after A or the spoken word the curtain falls on)

notes.FROM: null: the copy wears whatever look was on screen the frame before A (read off the timeline), or a CSS filter
notes.T: cue is a beat (seconds after A or a word, e.g. 'dark'); fall and close are lengths in seconds
notes.GRAIN: 0.18 reads as film, not noise, on a phone; keep it under 0.25

needs: GRADES: ({@T.cue}, {end}, "moody") or another look, starting on the curtain's first frame and running to B or later
typical_length: 5.6 s (the curtain itself is 0.3 s; the grain and vignette hold to B)
